acceptance_criteria: Future throttle timestamps never authorize ordinary suppression and are classified under one bounded clock-discontinuity policy shared by load, in-memory decisions, persistence, and episode accounting.
Same-process suppression eligibility and episode duration use monotonic time, while separately named wall-clock metadata cannot produce negative duration or extend suppression after rollback.
Restart after a write-then-rollback sequence follows an explicit bounded wall-clock policy and emits one metadata-only skew onset and one verified recovery transition.
Forward jumps expire or reclassify entries deterministically without duplicate episode transitions.
Recovery, source supersession, and asset removal close the exact suppression episode immediately with a typed bounded reason rather than waiting for another alert attempt or poller shutdown.
Removing and re-adding the same asset or source starts a new episode identity and count, and independent keys remain independent.

Missing, corrupt, unreadable, and future-skewed throttle state uses the vocabulary coordinated with issues #2447, #2533, and #2534 without absorbing their separately owned availability or reset contracts.
The merged O(1) entry and summary behavior, fifteen-minute normal delivery throttle, logged-out bypass, recovery behavior, supersession, and alert acceptance semantics remain unchanged.

Focused tests cover small and extreme future offsets, backward and forward jumps, restart, recovery before expiry, source supersession, asset removal, remove and re-add, shutdown, and independent keys.
Diagnostics contain only bounded reason classes, counts, and age or skew buckets and never contain stored keys, raw timestamps, identities, paths, payloads, commands, errors, targets, or topology.
blast_radius: Fleet alert-throttle eligibility across restart and clock discontinuity; suppression-episode duration, recovery, source supersession, asset removal, remove and re-add, shutdown summaries, and bounded operator diagnostics.

falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The residual finding is falsified if the pinned store rejects or explicitly bounds future timestamps, the poller cannot suppress on negative elapsed time, same-process duration is monotonic, and every recovery, supersession, and asset-removal transition immediately closes the matching episode. Exact source inspection and the future-entry canary disproved those conditions. This bounded record did not recreate the removed audit-only poller recovery canary or run a full fault-injection matrix, so negative-duration, restart, lifecycle-exit, privacy, and mutation coverage remain implementation-time verification obligations; the 157 green cited tests establish current behavior rather than correctness of the reopened invariants.
impact: A valid timestamp left in the future after wall-clock rollback can suppress an alert far beyond the declared fifteen-minute interval, an open episode can publish negative duration, and recovery or asset removal can leave stale per-key state resident until shutdown or later key reuse, merging logically separate suppression episodes and misrepresenting active suppression.

partial_findings.summary: Future timestamps remain fresh under one-sided subtraction, negative elapsed time suppresses normally, and episode duration uses rollback-sensitive wall time.
Merged PR #2389 bounds normal rate-limit and silence suppression logging to one entry and one bounded exit summary per episode.
Healthy recovery, source supersession, and asset removal do not immediately close or dispose the matching process-local suppression episode.

pull_request_overlaps.title: fix(fleet): bound alert-suppression logging to state transitions (#2355)

suggested_remediation: Define one typed throttle-clock classifier that is shared by store load, persistence, and poller decisions; use injected monotonic time for same-process eligibility and duration, apply a bounded explicit wall-clock policy after restart, and route recovery, supersession, removal, reason change, expiry, and shutdown through one typed episode-close operation. Preserve the merged O(1) logging and ordinary alert-delivery semantics while adding bounded metadata-only skew and lifecycle transition evidence.
title: reliability(fleet): alert-suppression episodes mishandle clock skew and lifecycle exits
